title: Vacuum decay
summary: Measured Higgs boson and top quark masses suggest our vacuum may be metastable: not the lowest energy state. A bubble of true vacuum could form by quantum tunnelling and expand at nearly light speed, destroying everything it reaches. Calculations within the Standard Model put the expected lifetime vastly beyond the current age of the universe.
support_note: A standard calculation if no new physics changes the Higgs potential.
what_happens: A tiny bubble of true vacuum nucleates
Its wall accelerates to nearly light speed
Inside, physics and chemistry change, so matter as we know it cannot exist
No warning arrives before the wall itself
objections: New physics beyond the Standard Model could stabilise the vacuum

sources.title: Gravitational effects on and of vacuum decay
